ai.definition: AI Agents are software entities designed to perform a wide range of complex tasks autonomously, interact with human users, and adapt their behavior based on the context and user feedback.
ai.howItWorks: AI Agents leverage machine learning algorithms, natural language processing (NLP), and other AI techniques to understand user inputs, process information, make decisions, and execute tasks. They can learn from interactions over time, improving their performance and responsiveness.
ai.problemSolved: Automating complex tasks that require human-like interaction and decision-making, reducing the need for manual intervention in various applications such as customer service, personal assistance, and home automation.
ai.manufacturing: Development through software engineering practices, including coding, testing, and deployment. No physical manufacturing involved.
ai.buildProcess: Involves defining the problem, selecting appropriate algorithms and models, training the AI agent using data, integrating with user interfaces, and continuously testing and refining the system based on performance metrics and user feedback.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Growing adoption in various industries with increasing complexity of tasks. Expected to become more integrated into everyday life as technology advances.
ai.regulation: Varies by jurisdiction, but generally requires compliance with data privacy laws, ethical guidelines for AI use, and specific industry regulations (e.g., healthcare, finance).
ai.profitability: Depends on the application; can be highly profitable in sectors where automation reduces costs or increases efficiency, but initial development costs may be high.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected to see advancements in explainable AI, more sophisticated NLP capabilities, and integration with other emerging technologies like IoT and robotics.

glossary.def: A software entity capable of performing complex tasks autonomously and interacting with users.
A subset of AI that involves training models on data to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed.
The field of AI focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.

subsystems.name: Interface and perception
subsystems.role: takes in user input and turns it into a form the agent can reason about.

subsystems.name: Language model core
subsystems.role: the reasoning engine that understands intent and generates plans and responses.

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: stores past interactions and retrieves relevant knowledge.

subsystems.name: Planning and decision-making
subsystems.role: breaks goals into steps and chooses which action to take next.

subsystems.name: Tool use and action
subsystems.role: executes actions in the world beyond text generation.

subsystems.name: Safety and governance
subsystems.role: keeps the agent within ethical and operational limits.

buildSteps.title: Define scope and success criteria
buildSteps.detail: Decide exactly which tasks the agent may perform, what autonomy it has, and how success and failure are measured.

buildSteps.title: Select or train a foundation model
buildSteps.detail: Choose a pre-trained language model or train one on domain data, then fine-tune it to follow instructions and call tools.

buildSteps.title: Design the agent architecture
buildSteps.detail: Combine planning, memory and tool modules into a loop, and specify how the language model invokes each one.

buildSteps.title: Implement tool integrations
buildSteps.detail: Connect APIs, databases and code execution environments with clear permission boundaries so the agent cannot act outside its remit.

buildSteps.title: Build memory and retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Set up vector databases and context management so the agent remembers relevant past interactions and looks up current facts.

buildSteps.title: Add safety and governance layers
buildSteps.detail: Insert guardrails, content filters and logging, and define which actions require human approval before execution.

buildSteps.title: Train for reasoning and tool use
buildSteps.detail: Use reinforcement learning from human feedback and simulated environments to improve multi-step problem solving and reliable tool calls.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and red-team
buildSteps.detail: Test in sandboxed scenarios for reliability, bias, security holes and failure modes before any real deployment.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with monitoring and oversight
buildSteps.detail: Run in production with continuous logging, performance tracking and human review of critical decisions.

prerequisites.why: they provide the core language understanding and generation that agents build on.
it aligns model outputs with human preferences and improves multi-step reasoning.
they give agents long-term memory and access to external knowledge beyond their training data.
many services still lack safe, uniform interfaces for autonomous agents to call.
we cannot yet guarantee an agent's goals remain aligned with human values as it acts autonomously over long periods.
training and running large agents requires substantial accelerator capacity and memory.

pathway.milestone: narrow agents for specific tasks, such as coding assistants and customer-service bots, that use tools but need close human supervision
multi-step autonomous agents that can plan and execute complex workflows with human-in-the-loop approval
pathway.unlocks: automation of multi-stage business and research processes.

pathway.milestone: self-improving agents that learn from experience and coordinate in multi-agent systems
pathway.unlocks: adaptive problem-solving and division of labour among specialised agents.

pathway.milestone: self-sustaining agents with robust ethical governance and alignment guarantees
pathway.unlocks: reliable autonomous operation in high-stakes environments, if alignment is solved.
